predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Bahrayn: Abu Sa'id al-Jannabi 'captured Bahrain's capital Hajr and al-Hasa in 899, which he made the capital of his state' (Qarmatians page)

successors.name: Uyunid Emirate
successors.text: Bahrain, al-Qatif and al-Hasa: the Uyunid page says Abdullah bin Ali Al Uyuni 'defeated the Qarmatians in Bahrain' in 1077-1078, with Seljuk help; the infobox founding is 1076

ledger.x: 899: Abu Sa'id al-Jannabi founds the Qarmatian state in Bahrayn.
900: the Abbasids send an army against the Qarmatians.
903: Hajar surrenders and the Qarmatians hold Bahrayn.
968: the Ikhshidid governor of Syria and Palestine becomes the Qarmatians' tributary.
970: the Fatimid takeover ends the tribute.
971: the Qarmatians and the Fatimids fight for Syria and Palestine.
1067: the Uyunid-Seljuk campaign against the last Qarmatian ground begins.

wars.name: Abbasid campaigns against Abu Sa'id al-Jannabi
wars.outcome: The Abbasid army under al-Abbas ibn Amr al-Ghanawi (2,000 soldiers with volunteers) was defeated on 31 July 900 near Qatif (al-Ghanawi captured, then released); Hajar, captured after the 900 victory, was lost again in 901 and surrendered anew in 903; the lead…

wars.name: Qarmatian raids on Iraq and the pilgrim road
wars.outcome: Raids without lasting ground: the Hajj caravan ambushed in 906 ('massacred 20,000 pilgrims'), Basra raided in 912 and from 923, Kufa raided in 927 with an Abbasid army beaten, Baghdad threatened in 928 (the page dates it 928; the Qarmatians page says the…

wars.name: Qarmatian sack of Mecca
wars.outcome: Abu Tahir sacked Mecca in 930 (the pages give no month) and carried the Black Stone to al-Ahsa; 'Attempts by the Abbasids and Fatimids to persuade him to return the Black Stone were rejected'; the Abbasids paid a large sum and it was returned in 952.

wars.name: Fatimid-Qarmatian wars in Syria and Egypt
wars.outcome: After taking Damascus from the Ikhshidid governor in 968 al-A'sam invaded Egypt in 971 and 974 and was beaten in two battles on 22 and 24 December 971 (the Fatimids had dug in at Ayn Shams) and at Jubb Umayra on 27 April 974; he died at Ramla in March 977; in…

wars.name: Abbasid defeat of the Qarmatians
wars.outcome: 'After their defeat by the Abbasids in 976, the Qarmatians began to look inwards' (Qarmatians page); the place and the Buyid share are not given.

wars.name: Uyunid and Seljuk conquest of al-Hasa
wars.outcome: Abdullah bin Ali Al Uyuni, with Seljuk Turks, besieged Hofuf for seven years and ended the Qarmatian state (1077-1078 on the Uyunid page).

certainty.note: Desert-oasis and coastal frontiers of eastern Arabia; none is fixed by treaty or survey.
